To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in unselected ED patients with suspected acute myocardial infaction (AMI) the diagnostic performances of a new high sensitivity cardiac troponin test and a standard cardiac troponin (cTnT or TnI) test for AMI diagnosis do not differ significantly and that the new high‐sensitivity cTnT test detects significantly more patients with other cardiac diseases.
the diagnostic performances of the hs‐cTNI and standard cTNI for AMI diagnosis were similar in unselected patients in the ED.

high‐sensitivity troponin T and standard troponin T have similar diagnostic performance for acute myocardial injury, but high‐sensitivity testing detects significantly more patients with acute or chronic cardiac disease.

the development of a high sensitivity cardiac troponin test (hs‐c‐TnT) for the detection of myocardial infarctions.

the question: “Is the new high‐sensitivity cTnT test superior to the current troponin T test in diagnosing myocardial infarctions in patients presenting with chest pain or other cardiac symptoms in an emergency room setting?”

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hs‐cTNT is a better cardiac marker for diagnosis of cardiac diseases, but not for AMI, in unselected ED patients.
hs‐cTNT and standard cTNT are not different in their ability to detect AMI in an emergency department.
hs‐cTNT does not add significantly to the diagnostic performance of cTNT in the ED, but that it does add to the detection of cardiac disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hs-cTnT and s-cTnT were both sensitive and specific markers for AMI.
the diagnostic performances of high sensitivity cardiac troponin and standard cTinT for AMI are comparable in everyday practice.
high sensitivity cardiac troponin testing did not add much in the diagnosis of acute myocardial infraction and in the prediction of mortality in emergency department.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hs‐cTNT is not superior to standard cTNT in the diagnosis of myocardial infarctions.
the clinical utility of high sensitivity troponin testing for the detection of myocardial injury is limited by the fact that the test is not specific for acute myocardial injury.
